captions.instagram:
How do avalanches happen?

A snowy slope is a stack of layers, and one weak layer can let the whole slope go. Dig a snow pit, turn round grains into sugar with a cold night, load a slab until a crack races across it, release an avalanche at over 100 km/h, and learn why the first fifteen minutes decide a rescue.

→ A snowy slope is not one blanket. Every storm of the winter leaves its own layer.
→ Dig a pit and you find the danger: a stiff slab resting on a thin, weak layer.
→ Thin snow on a bitterly cold night: vapour rises through it and turns round grains into loose sugar.
→ The slab’s weight pulls along the slope. Only the weak layer’s strength holds it back.
→ When the pull wins, a crack races through the weak layer and the whole slab breaks away.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/avalancheclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How do avalanches happen? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A snowy slope is a stack of layers, and one weak layer can let the whole slope go. Dig a snow pit, turn round grains into sugar with a cold night, load a slab until a crack races across it, release an avalanche at over 100 km/h, and learn why the first fifteen minutes decide a rescue.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/avalancheclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/avalancheclear

In this video:
• A mountain of layers. A snowpack is a stack of layers, one from every storm, each changed by wind, sun and cold.
• The weak layer. The ground under snow stays near 0 °C and the surface follows the air.
• The slab lets go. The slab's weight pulls along the slope with a stress of mass × gravity × sine of the angle.
• Triggers. A trigger adds load or removes strength: heavy snowfall, wind piling snow on the lee side of a ridge, rapid warming or rain, a cornice fall, a person, or an explosive fired on purpose.
• In motion. Loose-snow avalanches fan out from a point, slabs break as a plate, wet avalanches are slow and dense.
• The Himalaya, and staying safe. India's avalanche country is the high Himalaya and Karakoram, from Siachen and Gurez to Lahaul, Uttarakhand and Sikkim.
